facts.raw_span: progressive unilateral skin hardening on his right thigh and buttock for 7 years
motion of his right limb joint was slightly limited
ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal results for routine blood tests
Normal results for autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Demonstrated slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality

Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Negative Alcian blue staining

concepts.why: The patient's progressive unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined stony-hard plaque, and loss of skin elasticity are consistent with scleroderma, which is supported by the histopathological findings of dense reticular dermis and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis.

The patient's skin hardening, hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation are consistent with lipodermatosclerosis, which is supported by the imaging studies showing thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality.
The patient's histopathological findings of dense reticular dermis, increased expression of CD34, and subtle increase in density of fibroblasts are consistent with fibrosing dermopathy.

The patient's skin hardening, hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation are consistent with panniculitis, although the lack of inflammation in the histopathological findings makes this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F01: Progressive unilateral skin hardening is more typical of scleroderma and fibrosing dermopathy.
rationales.F03: The presence of a stony-hard plaque with loss of skin elasticity is highly suggestive of scleroderma and fibrosing dermopathy.
rationales.F07: Slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality can be seen in scleroderma, lipodermatosclerosis, and fibrosing dermopathy.
rationales.F08: The histopathological findings of normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts are consistent with scleroderma and fibrosing dermopathy.
rationales.F09: Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages is a characteristic feature of scleroderma and fibrosing dermopathy.
rationales.F10: Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis is a feature that can be seen in scleroderma and fibrosing dermopathy.
